values: The work models IoT measurements with SAREF (saref:Measurement, saref:hasValue, saref:isMeasuredIn), not SOSA/SSN; SOSA is only compared and declared as a prefix.
Observations are subclassed per sensing modality and per satellite product (GIFAPAR_S3_Observation); sosa:Platform declared a subclass of geosparql:Feature.
Zones and devices are subclasses of a platform and nest through sosa:hosts; quality indicators are attached to observations or sensors.
Features of a cyber-threat ontology are mapped to SOSA classes (Observation, Actuation, Procedure, Platform).
Social media posts are modelled as observations made by users as sensors.
Observations are also EWE events and actuations EWE actions (vlctas:ObservedEvent, vlctas:TriggeredAction) for rule-based automation; the property class is both observable and actuatable.
Sensor capabilities with ssn-system:Accuracy, Resolution and Condition using schema:unitCode; thresholds attached to carrier properties and SPARQL rules annotating exceedances.

A merged vehicle observation carries several values (speed, acceleration) through subproperties of hasSimpleResult; road sections are a subclass of sosa:Sample linked by a subproperty of sosa:hasSample.
The feature of interest of fault-detection observations is a sensor itself; actuations produce system states with own timespans, inserted by SPARQL Update rules.
Sensors and actuators are linked to AADL device components, and SWRL rules characterise them.
Rules infer a characteristic index (NDVI, NDWI) of an image from the bands it observes; CharacteristicIndex is an ssn:Property that is not observable.

Continuous sensing and actuation activities (ado:SensingActivity) are linked by own properties instead of sosa:observedProperty / madeBySensor, to avoid being inferred as observations; sensors and actuators are aligned as ep-plan:Agent.
Uses SSN 2011: one observation has several results typed by the quantity (CloudCover, AtmosphPress) instead of an observed property.
The manufacturer's normal output range is an ssn-system:MeasurementRange capability; a robot path is a procedure linked to the sensor by ssn:implements, used to choose a fallback sensor.
Instrument interfaces are platforms that host sensors and actuators, while the instrument links its components by an own property.
Sensors are omitted when no data layer describes them; observations are validated with generic SOSA-SHACL shapes.
Property chains compose sosa:hasFeatureOfInterest with spatial relations to S2 grid cells, which act as features for gridded data.
Observable properties carry the file locations of acceptance limits and results; observations link to test reports by an own property.
Observations (user inputs or meter readings) feed a PROV chain of emission calculation steps; the quantity kind sits on the result rather than an observed property.
The hall is at once a sample of the building, a feature of interest and a platform hosting the sensor board.
Uses SSN 2011: a measurement (control point) observation has per-phenomenon observations as parts via dul:hasPart.
Observations are the data source of KPI calculations; sensors are left out of the model.
A sosa:Result may be an RDF graph description presented with lifting, lowering and validation rules; WoT TD terms are aligned as subclasses and subproperties of SSN system and procedure terms.

In a MERODE domain model, a Device class generalises Sensor and Actuator and a Device Usage class generalises Observation, Actuation and Sampling; an own Platform Deployment ties a platform to one feature of interest.
Observations declare neither unit nor observed property; both are factored on the sosa:ObservationCollection they belong to.
Rules over observations derive new facts (off-limit areas); an observation result can be a person IRI.
The feature of interest is used to hold the sensor and actuator limits and faulty patterns against which observations are compared; Sampling stores observations over a period.
The patient is the feature of interest of the observations, queried through sosa:isFeatureOfInterestOf.
SSN 2011-based observation capability ontology: sensors subclassed into remote and in-situ sensors, linked to tasks and ssn:Stimulus as DUL events.
Own System, Sensor and Actuator classes subclass the SOSA ones, with system components, states, and operating conditions declared subclasses of a sosa:Condition class that SOSA does not define.
Terms are invented in the ssn namespace: ssn:Temperature, ssn:WindSpeed, ssn:relativehumidity as datatype properties.
sosa:Sensor is declared a subclass of bot:Element so rooms contain sensors; evolving room properties use OPM property states.
Uses SSN 2011 with equivalence axioms to PROV-O (ssn:Observation as prov:Entity, ssn:Process as prov:Activity) so a reasoner materialises provenance.
Only sosa:Procedure and ssn:System are reused, as concepts of a civil complaint ontology for digital-twin government.
The kind of measurement is given by the type of the result node (HeartRateObservationValue) rather than an observed property.
Smart-building algorithms (forecasting, MPC) are subclasses of sosa:Procedure, with their inputs and outputs as subclasses of ssn:Input and ssn:Output linked to Brick sensors.
Datasets are modelled as collections of virtual entities whose primary source is a sensor, linked with PROV-O activities such as measurement campaigns.
Test messages use non-standard SSN terms (ssn:hasID, ssn:hasUnit with qu:DegreeCelsius) as inputs to an automatic mapping system.
An ssn:Deployment stands for a building and is linked to beacons by an own namespace property rather than ssn:deployedSystem.
Quality-of-observation attributes and effects are attached to SSN 2011 measurement capabilities.
Controllers and predictors implement procedures (pep:implements) and optimise properties of HVAC spaces as features of interest.
Domain classes are placed under BFO, QUDT, SOSA and MASON parents; process parameters are QUDT quantity kinds while measured quantities are observable properties.
Spatial relations link sensors, observable properties and bridge components, with space types from SPOT.
A GraphQL interface navigates platform, hosts, madeObservation; the room itself is the platform.
Sensed data are drone:MissionSensorData mission event elements rather than sosa:Observation.
The observation pattern is collapsed into one predicate per property and result time (averageHeatingDegreeDaysPerMonthAug2021) pointing directly to the simple result.
SOSA terms are used as NGSI-LD relationships in JSON-LD entities alongside SAREF4EE and M3-lite properties.
sosa:Observation and saref:Measurement are mapped to the work's own observation and measurement classes for construction quality inspection.
A holdsState data property on the dynamic vehicle property gives the current value without instantiating a sosa:Observation.
Stream payload fields are linked to a sosa:Property (a term SOSA does not define) to tie stream schemas to system capabilities.
IoT sensors themselves are said to act as features of interest for observation and actuation.
